questions.question: What is the first physical unit produced by blocked index construction?
options: A sorted immutable run built within a memory budget
One globally mutable postings file edited in place
A dense term-document matrix for the full corpus
A merged dictionary covering every input block

questions.question: In what order are occurrence records sorted?
options: Document ID, term, position
Term, document ID, position
Term, position, document ID
Position, term, document ID

options: cloud->[1]

questions.topic: Blocked Index Construction: Build Runs, Merge Runs
questions.question: Why should workers use deterministic document IDs?
options: Local counters coordinate globally without any communication
Document IDs are stripped out before the postings are merged
Differing IDs improve detection of duplicate source documents
Independent counters can collide or make replays differ

questions.topic: Blocked Index Construction: Build Runs, Merge Runs
questions.question: What makes an immutable run useful for failure recovery?
options: A committed checksum-validated run can be reused by a retry
Readers consume it safely while its bytes are still changing
It removes the need to record input scope or analyzer version
A partial write counts as equivalent to a complete run

questions.topic: Blocked Index Construction: Build Runs, Merge Runs
questions.question: Why should final validation reconcile source and index counts?
options: A readable dictionary proves every input block was included
A structurally valid index can still omit a whole source block
Postings counts are unrelated to construction completeness
Checksums guarantee that rejected documents were indexed

questions.question: What triggers a logarithmic merge to the next level?
options: A query arrives containing more than one search term
A document is rescored after its content changes
A new segment collides with an occupied size level
A reader opens the manifest of the current index

questions.question: With geometrically sized levels, how many occupied segments exist in the simple model?
options: O(N squared)
Exactly N
O(sqrt N)
O(log N)

questions.question: Base batch size is 1,000. What happens when the fourth batch arrives after two batches already formed level 1 and batch three occupies level 0?
options: Level 0 merges up and carries into a 4,000-document level 2
All four batches stay independent at level 0 indefinitely
The first three batches are deleted, leaving only batch four
Every source document is reindexed under the new analyzer

questions.question: How are deletes represented before a merge removes old postings physically?
options: As negative document frequencies in every dictionary
As tombstones that suppress older document versions
As holes punched into the compressed postings bytes
As gaps rewritten into every surviving postings list

questions.question: Why must a merge commit use a generation-aware manifest?
options: To block new documents until every reader has terminated
To overwrite newer segments created after the snapshot
To replace merged inputs while keeping concurrent segments
To expose the new segment before its output is durable

questions.question: What is the main cost of delaying background merges too long?
options: Source documents become impossible to tokenize
Stable document IDs change on every incoming query
Every index write becomes globally transactional
Segment fan-out and stale bytes accumulate

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: What is a major correctness benefit of a full rebuild?
options: It re-derives coherent state from the authoritative corpus
It always provides lower update latency than a small segment
It avoids reading source documents or analyzer configuration
It preserves every historical tombstone and obsolete posting

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: What is a major benefit of incremental merging?
options: It removes all segment and version-management complexity
It absorbs small changes without rewriting the whole corpus
It guarantees that old analyzer generations stay usable
It makes periodic source reconciliation unnecessary

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: A 50,000-document policy corpus changes weekly and rebuilds in four minutes. Which choice is strongest?
options: Permanent merge machinery regardless of operational cost
One mutable postings file edited in place during serving
Simple versioned full replacement with shadow validation
Weekly tombstones with no reconciliation against source

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: Why does a new tokenizer generally require a complete new index version?
options: Tokenization changes only the display text after retrieval
Old postings can infer new token boundaries without the source
Mixed analyzer generations guarantee identical statistics
The analyzer changes keys, postings, positions, and statistics

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: When can a large deletion wave favor rebuilding?
options: When emitting live data beats carrying tombstones through merges
When no source record identifies which documents remain live
When deleted documents must stay visible to every live query
When the rebuild output cannot be versioned or published atomically

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: What hybrid policy balances freshness and drift control?
options: Full rebuild after every document, with no incremental segments
Incremental segments and merges plus periodic reconciliation
Unlimited segments with no compaction or source comparison
In-place file mutation without manifests or rollback versions
